source.title: Optimal Representation Size: High-Dimensional Analysis of Pretraining and Linear Probing
source.authors: Valentina Njaradi; C. Dominé; Rachel Swanson; Marco Mondelli; Andrew M. Saxe

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: It analyzes double descent in pretrained linear regression as retained representation dimension changes, using PCA followed by downstream regression rather than the original deep-network size sweep.
record.gate_note: The paper directly reports a double-descent curve in theoretical and simulated generalisation error over retained representation size in a specified regime. Its Pythia experiments measure validation accuracy over PCA component count and describe dimension-dependent optima, not model-size or epoch-wise test-error double descent. The paper does not report that adding training samples near interpolation raises test error. Cited double-descent results are not extracted as this study's results.
record.test_reason: The paper derives and simulates a double-descent generalisation curve over retained representation fraction α in PCA-pretrained linear regression. Double descent appears when n_l < p, with the peak at the interpolation point γ_eff = αγ_l = 1. This is a new linear model class and complexity axis, not a re-run of the original deep-network protocol, so T3 fits better than T2.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors' main conclusion concerns optimal representation size. Tuning PCA dimension improves downstream generalisation. Maximal compression is optimal when pretraining data is abundant and labelled data scarce; higher dimension is better when pretraining data is limited. There is an exact trade-off between unlabelled and labelled samples, and similar phenomenology appears in autoencoders and Pythia. Double descent is a secondary analytic feature: the variance term peaks at γ_eff = 1, and choosing α mitigates it without explicit regularization.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses independent unlabelled PCA pretraining followed by downstream linear regression, and varies retained representation dimension. It does not reproduce the original deep-network model-size, epoch, or sample-size sweeps.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported optimal representation size and phase boundaries depend on pretraining and downstream sample sizes, signal-to-noise ratio, spike strength, and task alignment. The double-descent peak is expressed through γ_eff = αγ_l.

fits_no_version.finding: Pythia-70M-deduped SST-2 linear probes: validation accuracy over PCA dimension m peaks at intermediate m for small n_l and rises monotonically for large n_l.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The optimal linear-probe representation dimension in pretrained transformers depends on downstream dataset size and pretraining duration.

record.problems: The main theory uses a stylized rank-one spiked-covariance model and PCA followed by linear regression. The transformer experiments use one 70M-parameter model family and validation accuracy over representation dimension, not test error over model size or epochs. The paper does not test whether adding downstream samples near interpolation raises error, nor whether optimal regularization removes the peak.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-version results were left out. Autoencoder results concern optimal bottleneck dimensions and do not report the specified double-descent curve; cited findings from other work were excluded.

untested.parts: No sweep of deep-network model size.
No test error over training epochs; Pythia checkpoints index pretraining data, not epoch-wise test error.
Varying n_l shifts the interpolation threshold (Fig. 5 b,f), but the paper never reports that adding labelled samples raises test error at fixed α.
Epoch and model-size axes; no single complexity measure is tested across those axes.
Multiple/triple descent; whether optimally tuned ridge removes the peak (ridge is listed as future work).

missing.what: Varying downstream sample size n_l shifts the location of the interpolation-threshold peak along α (Fig. 5 b,f). This is relevant to whether the peak tracks γ_eff (V5) and to the sample axis (V3).
When γ_l < 1 the generalisation error has a single minimum with no double descent, and in the limit γ_l → 0 double descent disappears. In both cases γ_eff never reaches the interpolation point 1.
missing.locator: Section 4.2 (Corollary 2 discussion, limit γ_l → 0); Appendix A.9, Eq. (43); Fig. 5(e,g,h)

record.verdict_notes: Neither original source is this paper. Belkin et al. is cited as [34], and Gedon et al. 'No double descent in PCR' is cited only. Tranche changed from T2 to T3 because the setting (PCA-pretrained linear regression, α axis) is a new model class rather than a different method on the original deep-network question. The double descent here is the known least-squares interpolation peak at m = n_l, transplanted to a pretrained subspace.

versions.untested_parts: No sweep of deep-network model size or parameter count.
No test-error curve over training epochs; checkpoints are used to examine representation dimensionality and validation accuracy.

The paper varies downstream sample size and reports shifts in the interpolation threshold and optimal representation size, but does not report increased test error from adding data near that threshold.
The double-descent result is established for the paper's pretrained linear-regression setting; it does not establish the curve across model classes generally.
The paper relates the representation-size curve to the effective aspect ratio γ_eff = αγ_l; it does not test a shared predictor of peak location across model size, epochs, and sample size.
The paper derives a double-descent variance contribution, but does not test multiple/triple descent or whether optimally tuned regularization removes the peak.
No comparison that recounts complexity using an alternative effective parameter count and tests whether the curve becomes an ordinary U-shape.

rows.subject: pretrained regression (PCA representation followed by linear regression)
rows.size_stated: High-dimensional asymptotic regime: p/n_l → γ_l, p/n_u → γ_u, m/p → α; simulations use p = 500.
rows.stage_stated: Unlabelled PCA pretraining followed by downstream linear regression.
rows.operation_detail: Sweep the retained representation fraction α = m/p and measure generalisation error.
rows.measure: Generalisation error versus retained representation size.
rows.value: The generalisation error exhibits double descent, with two local minima; the reported peak is at α ≈ 1/γ_l.
rows.uncertainty: not stated for the asymptotic result; Figure 5 simulations show empirical mean ± one standard deviation across trials.
rows.note: The paper describes two minima in this regime and gives the peak location relative to γ_l. This is a retained-representation-dimension sweep, not a deep-network parameter-count sweep.
rows.check: Values are correct. Two local minima (α=1 and small α) and a peak at α ≈ 1/γ_l, i.e. γ_eff = 1, the point where m = n_l and training error reaches zero (Theorem 3). Bears on V5 only for the α and n_l axes, not epochs or model size.

source_check.locator_found: Section 4.2, discussion preceding Corollary 1; Appendix B.1, Figure 5 discussion; Section 3 and Theorem 3.
